business_scope.primary_industry_name: Assembly of Bionic Companion Robotic Animals with Speech Synthesizers

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Latin European heritage) with selected Common Law elements in commercial and maritime practice; private interest foundations governed by special private statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty Panama–United States (in force 1991)
United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT), as amended by Law 70 of 2019; Law 254 of 27 August 2021 (UBO Register and corporate reforms); Executive Decree 363 of 2021 (UBO registration regulations); UAF Agreement 2021-04 (binding due-diligence rules for obliged non-financial entities); Registro Público tariff and registration compilation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notaría Pública del Circuito (Panama City or place of execution)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notaría Pública of the executing notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of the founder, council members, protector, and beneficiaries against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panamanian national designations (UAF/CNE); enhanced due diligence for PEPs, including foreign PEPs, per UAF Agreement 2021-04 and Law 254 of 2021; documented source of wealth required for contributions above USD 50,000; negative-news and adverse-media check as standard practice.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (SIRP: Sistema de Información del Registro Público), https://www.registro.com.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name may be in Spanish or any Latin-script language but must contain the token 'Fundación' or 'Foundation'; non-Latin scripts must be submitted with an official transliteration into Spanish characters; the Registry rejects names identical or phonetically confusing with existing registered entities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A single 30-day extension may be requested through SIRP before expiry. If the reservation is rejected, the applicant may file a Recurso de Reconsideración before the Registro Público within 5 business days and a Recurso de Apelación before the administrative appellate authority within 10 business days; in practice, refiling with a corrected name (adding 'Fundación' and removing phonetic conflicts) yields clearance within 24–48 hours.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not recognized for PIF registration: Law 25 of 1995 requires a resident agent with a physical street address in Panama; a PO Box, virtual mail address, or purely digital office cannot satisfy the registered-office requirement for a Private Interest Foundation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (≈3%): the Registro Público performs desk-based compliance reviews and selective verification; UAF conducts on-site AML inspections at the resident agent's office rather than the foundation's premises; inspection risk rises only if the foundation undertakes physical commercial activity in Panama without a municipal Aviso de Operación.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), Articles 1-42, as amended; complemented by Law 23 of 2015 on Beneficial Owner Registry and Executive Decrees on resident agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section), with mandatory prior notarial protocol.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional) executed as a public deed before a Panamanian Notary Public and presented for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Foundation Charter must allocate an identifiable initial endowment, commonly US$10,000, to the Foundation. The endowment is not escrowed or subject to withdrawal restrictions and may be held in a foundation bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Founder and initial Council of [Name] Private Interest Foundation, acting under Law 25 of 1995, resolves: (1) To adopt the Foundation Charter and accept the initial endowment of US$10,000. (2) To establish the registered office in Panama City, Republic of Panama, at the Charter address. (3) To appoint the Resident Agent, Council Members, and Protector named in the Charter. (4) To register the Foundation with the Public Registry of Panama and authorize the Resident Agent to publish required notices and execute ancillary documents. (5) To open a US dollar account and file the RUC after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Commercial Names Section, and the Sede Electrónica online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name-search request to verify that the proposed foundation name containing 'Interactive AI Pet Robot' is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. If available, reserve the name for the foundation and obtain a name availability receipt from the registry cashier or online portal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name availability, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved by another entity, file an alternate name with a distinctive distinguishing number or element and re-submit the search without payment of a new service fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish, stating the foundation name, object including assembly of bionic companion robotic animals and speech synthesizers, initial endowment, Council members, Resident Agent, Protector, beneficiaries and rules of administration. The Founder and Council members must appear before the Notary to execute the public deed; the Notary will protocol the deed and issue authorized copies for registration.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of Founder and Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies defective clauses or missing signatures, cure the defect by submitting the corrected text, re-executing before the same Notary, and re-protocoling the deed before any registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Foundation at Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the protocoled Foundation Charter together with the Resident Agent acceptance and the sworn statement of lawful activity before the Public Registry. Pay the registry and stamp fees, either online through Sede Electrónica or in person at the registry cashier. After substantive examination, the registry will issue the Foundation Certificate evidencing juridical personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Notarial protocol
Resident Agent acceptance and address consent
Sworn declaration of compliance with beneficial owner rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a prevention or query, submit a written curable response within the applicable term, correct clerical or substantive points indicated, and if a Spanish translation of attached documents is required, file a certified Spanish translation and request reopening of the term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Certificate and Tax Registration (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Foundation Certificate is issued, obtain certified copies from the Registry. Proceed to DGI via its online taxpayer portal to register the Foundation as a juridical person, obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), and if applicable, register for notice of taxation status under the territorial tax system.
required_dossiers: Foundation Certificate issued by the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Resident Agent identity and address information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI requests additional background documentation or withholds the RUC, obtain a no-incumbency certificate from the Registry, clarify the beneficial owner structure, and re-submit through the DGI fiscal portal or at the attention window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama Beneficial Owner Registry, operated within the Dirección General de Ingresos / Unidad de Análisis Financiero
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the mandatory beneficial owner declaration within the legal period after registration, disclosing the Founder, Foundation Council Members, Protector, and any significant beneficial owners. Update the registry promptly upon any change in ownership or control. Obtain the electronic acknowledgement of the filing.
required_dossiers: Passports and tax identification of all beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Beneficial Owner Registry rejects or queries the filing, correct incomplete owner data or add missing official translations, and file the amended declaration within five business days to avoid late-filing penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Industrias; no statutory industrial license is required for low-risk ISIC 3240 robotic toy assembly under current industrial classification rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None mandatory; if local zoning or customs facilitation requires a municipal operating document, the applicable title is the 'Aviso de Operación' issued by the Mayoral Office of the district of operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Registration / Exempt, not a full Environmental Impact Assessment; the assembly of bionic companion robotic toys with hand tools, low-voltage electronics, and no industrial effluent is treated as low-impact under Law 41 of 1998.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater beyond ordinary sanitary discharge; comply with national effluent norms for sanitary sewers, occupational VOC exposure limits for soldering fluxes, municipal solid-waste collection rules, and universal-waste battery handling standards requiring disposal through authorized recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural load review of assembly racks and storage shelving; occupational health inspection by the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) covering electrical grounding, ventilation, emergency exits, noise exposure, and ergonomic workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama; portal: SIAF (Sistema Integrado de Administración de Ingresos) at https://siaf.dgi.gob.pa/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign entity (or its Panama resident agent) must first form or register the Panama vehicle with the Public Registry, then obtain an RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) with DGI through the SIAF online portal. For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), the RUC is only required once the foundation conducts taxable Panama-source activity, including exports. The RUC application requires drafting by a licensed attorney, authenticated public deed, proof of the resident agent, and email/digital signature activation for e-fiscal documents. The DGI will issue a 10-digit NIT/RUC number after verification; the municipal 'Aviso de Operación' must also be obtained before commencing local business operations. Exporters must additionally register with the DGI exporter registry and the Single Customs Window (SIGA) for submission of export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box election exists under Panama law; classification follows the governing Civil Code and the enabling law of the vehicle. A Private Interest Foundation is treated as a separate legal person but only taxed on Panama-source income; it may choose to distribute income to beneficiaries or to accumulate without changing this default classification. Hybrid mismatch elections are not applicable. For foreign tax purposes, a Panama PIF may, under U.S. check-the-box rules, be independently classified as a corporation or trust, but this election is not recognized in Panama and does not alter the domestic territorial tax result.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a value-added-type tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum turnover threshold; any person carrying out taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama, or importing goods, must register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer comprehensive regime (Régimen Simplizado de Pago) applies to taxpayers with annual gross income under B/.30,000 (approx. USD 30,000), which is optional and carries a fixed monthly quota.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has a mandatory phased electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica) system for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers. Issuers must obtain DGI pre-authorization for each invoice series through the SIAF web services; the generated XML invoice carries a QR code, fiscal digital stamp (barcode), and a registered cryptographic digital signature. No physical stamping is required, but invoices must be submitted electronically to DGI for validation and fiscal clearance. Large and medium taxpayers are required to integrate their billing systems with DGI's API (SIAF-Web Services), with enforcement and monitoring of non-compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Panama, including robotic AI pet toys assembled in Panama and sold to a customer resident abroad with physical delivery outside the Republic of Panama, are subject to ITBMS at 0% (zero-rated), provided the goods have left the customs territory under a valid export declaration and the sale is not to a Panama-resident intermediary. Services performed entirely abroad on behalf of non-residents are also zero-rated. The zero rating applies at the sale stage, and input ITBMS paid on materials, components, and local services attributable to export sales can be credited or refunded as 'credito fiscal' against the ITBMS settlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA)
Bill of Lading / Airwaybill / Certificado de Embarque
Commercial Invoice and e-invoiced counterpart (Factura Electrónica)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank Transfer/Payment Voucher evidencing receipt of proceeds from abroad
Proof of actual physical exit (Port/Customs Colonel receipt, DHL/FedEx waybill, or container seal log)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama Customs and DGI jointly audit export zero-rating claims for robotic toys and similar manufacturers. The exporter must maintain the complete export documentation bundle for 5 years (unless a longer audit extension is notified) and the proceeds must be repatriated to Panama within 180 days from shipment. Failure to demonstrate physical export via the DUA, Bill of Lading and bank corroboration will cause the ITBMS to be retroactively charged at the standard rate (7%) on the gross sale. Penalties include surcharges up to 30% of the omitted tax plus 10% of the original tax per month of delay; administrative fines range from B/.1,000 to B/.10,000 or up to 10 times the amount of the fraudulent credit; criminal tax fraud may result in imprisonment of 2 to 5 years. In a clawback, the exporter must return all refunded input VAT credits together with interest, and the refund bond or fiscal guarantee, if any, will be executed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama has no central bank, and the US dollar is the legal tender. The SBP regulates banking and official licensing, supported by the Ministry of Economy and Finance for monetary policy execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both capital and current accounts. Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with no exchange control regulations; profit remittance, dividends, and capital repatriation are unrestricted. Compliance burdens are limited to anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) documentation, tax filing under the territorial tax regime, and any sector-specific disclosure obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export receipts in Panama. Since the US dollar is legal tender, all export proceeds may be retained in USD bank accounts. Exporters must comply only with customs declaration procedures and maintain underlying bills of lading and commercial invoices for treasury and banking verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Cross-border Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for fully-regulated banking activity; Medium for ancillary payment facilitation. Panama lacks a dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licensing regime; nonbank digital wallets cannot operate as full banks. Offshore digital EMIs may be used for payment collection and cross-border disbursement support, but they cannot access Panama's local clearing network (ACH Panama/SIPA RTGS) and are subject to SBP innovation-hub review. Virtual asset service providers require prior SBP authorization under the Panamanian Crypto Law framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least the primary signatory and ultimate beneficial owner is generally required for the initial account opening interview at a Panamanian bank. Remote opening is possible on a case-by-case basis, requiring notarized and apostilled corporate documents, enhanced due diligence questionnaires, and a live video conference. For Private Interest Foundations (PIFs), the Founder and the initial Foundation Council member must physically execute banking forms, and the Protector (if appointed) must provide a certified identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the Private Interest Foundation's beneficiary structure (nominee council members and silent founder) raising underwriting red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter, Private Instrument of Foundation, beneficial ownership declaration, sworn statement from the Council member confirming legal capacity, full details of beneficiaries and Protector, and a written explanation of legitimate commercial purpose tied to the AI pet robot assembly venture.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds concerns for injection of capital to fund robotics hardware and cross-border component purchases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or certified financial statements, verifiable corporate bank statements from the originating account, third-party valuations of assets, tax returns (if resident), and a structured source-of-wealth breakdown demonstrating accumulated savings or transfers from lawful business operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent revenue pattern or high-volume credit-card collections flagged for the sale of interactive AI pet robots without a physical manufacturing facility in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly notarized commercial contracts with overseas contract manufacturers, freight forwarders, and fulfillment centers; bills of lading and logistics invoices; customs declarations; screenshot or export of processing statements from Stripe or card acquirers; description of the territorial tax treatment of manufacturing income under Panama's territorial regime and documentation proving substantive operational control in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire opacity or mismatched purpose codes in inbound remittances for the PIF's capital contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manual wire instructions with standardized purpose wording, FDI or consistent internal loan/capital contribution code, KYC/Tax Information Exchange forms completed by the remitting entity, signed investment declaration, and a consolidated flow chart of the funding chain from ultimate investor to PIF and then to the trading entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injection: (1) The originator sends a SWIFT MT103 from the corresponding bank to the Panamanian beneficiary bank using standard field 70 (Remittance Information) stating 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF (ISIC 3240) for interactive AI pet robot manufacturing and overseas component procurement'; (2) Provide supporting invoice or pro-forma contract, passport/ID of beneficial owner, foundation charter, and KYC declaration to the receiving bank; (3) The bank applies local AML screenings and may convert the credit to a capital escrow account before release; (4) Once cleared, funds become available in the PIF treasury and can be deployed under the corporate operating bank protocol.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement uses SWIFT MT103 for low-value supplies, MT202/MT202 COV for interbank funding legs, and commercial letters of credit (L/C) for structured large hardware purchases from international suppliers. For urgent Taiwan/China component settlements, the PIF may use SWIFT MT700 (documentary credit issuance) and MT710/MT720 confirmation. Domestic clearing for operational expenses in Panama runs through ACH Panamá and the SIPA RTGS system, while high-value dollar settlements require SBP banking coverage and strict reconciliation against the commercial invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated forward contracts (via Panamanian banks or offshore dealing desks)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for CNY/TWD/EUR cross-currency alignment, if Panamanian bank credit approval is obtained
Cross-currency swaps with a licensed international dealer or a SBP-regulated local bank
Commodity-linked adaptive pricing clauses embedded in purchase contracts to mitigate FX variance in supply-chain settlements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Annuity (Tasa Anual; Art. 36 Exec. Decree 15 of 28 Sep 1995, Law 25 of 1995 as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) via Banco Nacional de Panama; compliance marker recorded at the Public Registry of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January in each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% monthly late surcharge on the unpaid annuity; denial of certification; administrative strike-off after 3 consecutive years of non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Cumplimiento) issued after annuity payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Section of Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued within 1-3 business days after payment; valid until the next 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unavailable while annuity is unpaid; blocks banking transactions, notarial acts, and asset transfers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Report (Informe de Sustancia Economica) - Law 254 of 2019 / Decree 58 of 2021 [CONDITIONAL]
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) - Economic Substance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end only if the PIF performs a relevant activity in Panama; passive asset-holding PIFs with no Panamanian-source business are exempt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to US$50,000; false or incomplete declaration up to US$1,000,000; strike-off risk for repeated non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Record Annual Confirmation to the Registered Agent (Law 23 of 2015 and AML Resolution No. 142-2023)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panama registered agent; file maintained at the PIF office for inspection by DGI and UAF; no public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January together with the annuity; within 30 days of any change in founder, beneficiary, or council membership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML fines and criminal liability for false records; revocation of registered-agent license; freezing of foundation bank accounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit for Panama PIFs; audit is mandatory only if the foundation charter so requires, if DGI demands audited financial statements during an economic substance or tax examination, or if the foundation directly holds regulated financial entities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Law 25 of 1995 requires internal books evidencing financial position and transactions; Panama General Accounting Principles (PCGA) acceptable, IFRS recommended for cross-border financing; no filing of accounts with any Panama authority

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PIF has no shareholders; beneficial rights flow from the charter and regulations. By each 31 January the Foundation Council must reconfirm founder, council members, beneficiaries, and successor designations to the registered agent, which updates its Law 23 UBO file and presents it to DGI or UAF on demand. Any transfer of beneficial interest must be recorded in the council act book within 30 days
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of foundation act and charter as inscribed in the Public Registry
Book of acts and resolutions of the Foundation Council
Register of foundation patrimony (assets, contributions, disbursements)
Accounting records with supporting documentation; registered-agent UBO file

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250 - US$600 per year (registered office plus compliance support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not compulsory; voluntary audit US$2,500 - US$6,500; DGI-mandated audit US$5,000 - US$10,000
